title: Empowering Graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search with Adaptive Awareness Capabilities

problem.claim: Graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search faces local optima and redundant computations that limit query performance.

gap.claim: Existing methods do not fully exploit proximity-graph topology and suffer from distribution mismatches between base data and queries.

contributions.claim: GATE is a lightweight adaptive module for accelerating approximate nearest neighbor search on graph-based indexes.
GATE identifies query-specific entry points by extracting hub nodes and encoding graph structure with query-relevant features using a contrastive-learning two-tower model.
GATE constructs a navigation-graph index over candidate hub nodes to reduce model inference overhead.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GATE achieves a 1.2–2.0X query-performance speed-up over state-of-the-art graph-based indexes in extensive experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Approximate nearest neighbor search is widely used in high-dimensional applications.
Graph-based methods have strong query performance but face local optima, redundant computation, topology underuse, and base-query distribution mismatch.
GATE selects query-specific hub-node entry points, encodes topology and query features, and indexes the hubs for efficient navigation.
The authors report 1.2–2.0X query-performance speed-ups against state-of-the-art graph-based indexes.
